A 61-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a two-day history of progressively
worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and fever of 38.3°C (100.9°F). He has been
hospitalized twice in the past year for similar episodes. He has a 40-pack-year smoking history. Upon
examination, he is observed to be somewhat confused. He is dyspneic and can only speak 3-5 words
at a time before having to stop and gasp for air, which begins to improve after supplemental oxygen via
nasal cannula is supplied. On auscultation, wheezing and rhonchi are detected localized to the right
lower lung.  A chest X-ray shows increased lung volume, with the diaphragm appearing flattened and
low in position. The lung fields also appear more transparent than normal. Which of the following
abnormalities would be seen on his electrocardiogram (ECG)? Answer Choices: (A) Left bundle branch
block (B) A QT interval of 680 msec (C) Increase in P wave amplitude (D) Low voltage (E) Bifid P
waves (F) Right axis deviation with S1Q3T3 pattern (G) Right bundle branch block (H) Poor R wave
progression (I) ST segment depression in V1-V3 (J) Prominent U waves
 A. Left bundle branch block
B. Poor R wave progression
C. Bifid P waves
D. Right bundle branch block
E. Prominent U waves
F. Low voltage
G. Right axis deviation with S1Q3T3 pattern
H. A QT interval of 680 msec
I. ST segment depression in V1-V3
J. Increase in P wave amplitude
